summary: Each assertion performs one strict comparison and one fixed return-or-throw decision, matching the unavoidable constant work needed to produce an assertion outcome.

optimality.argument: Every assertion call must produce a boolean or error outcome, establishing an Omega(1) lower bound. Each accepted method performs one strict comparison followed by one fixed return or throw, giving O(1) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: Producing either required outcome needs at least one operation.
Both closure methods execute one strict comparison and one constant-size branch.
Cases cover both methods, both exact error messages, strict type distinctions, null, booleans, zero, and empty strings.
